//: The plugin's web half is browser code, so it is typechecked with browser
resolution rather than with the NodeNext settings the rest of examples/ uses.
This is not a preference. The repo-wide base is `moduleResolution: NodeNext`,
which REQUIRES a `.js` extension on every relative import. Turbopack bundles
these same files for the browser and does not map a `.js` specifier onto the
`.ts` file beside it, so a `.js` extension that satisfies tsc makes the Next
build fail with `Can't resolve`. The two cannot both be satisfied by one
specifier, so the file gets the resolution that matches where it runs.
`resolveExtensions` in next.config does NOT fix this — it chooses which
extensions to try for an extensionless import, not how to reinterpret one
that is already written. Verified, not assumed.
The runtime half keeps NodeNext: the API imports it under Bun, where the
`.js` specifiers are correct and load-bearing. Only `web/` moves.
Rooted at the repo root because these modules reach into apps/web and
packages/ by relative path, exactly as the parent project does.
//allowImportingTsExtensions: Same reason examples/tsconfig.json gives: packages/workflow-layout's modules import each other with explicit .ts, so pulling any of them in raises TS5097 on that package's INTERNAL specifiers — files this project does not own. Nothing here writes one.
//include: `.ts` only. The `.tsx` files here are React components that import apps/web
by relative path, so checking them needs that app's `@/*` paths and its CSS
module declarations — they are already covered by `typecheck:web`, which has
both. Only the `.ts` modules had the NodeNext-versus-Turbopack conflict this
project exists to resolve, so only they belong in it.
